subject: Ancient History
detail: Bhasa is one of the earliest known Sanskrit dramatists, placed roughly between the 2nd century BCE and the 3rd century CE. Kalidasa praises him in the Malavikagnimitra, and Banabhatta also mentions him. His plays were rediscovered in 1912 by T. Ganapati Sastri in Kerala, and are known as the Trivandrum plays. The thirteen plays include Svapnavasavadatta, Pratijnayaugandharayana, Charudatta, Avimaraka, Pratimanataka, Abhishekanataka, Balacharita, Dutavakya, Dutaghatotkacha, Karnabhara, Urubhanga, Pancharatra and Madhyama-vyayoga. Madhyama-vyayoga is a short one-act play based on a Mahabharata episode involving Bhima and Ghatotkacha. Elimination: Kavyalankara is a work of poetics by Bhamaha (about the 7th century CE). Natyashastra, the foundational treatise on dramaturgy, is attributed to Bharata Muni. Mahabhashya is Patanjali's commentary on Panini's Ashtadhyayi (about the 2nd century BCE). So only (c) is a play, and it is Bhasa's.
explanations: (a) Wrong: Kavyalankara is a treatise on poetics written by Bhamaha, not a play by Bhasa.
(b) Wrong: Natyashastra is the ancient treatise on drama, dance and music, attributed to Bharata Muni.
(c) Correct: Madhyama-vyayoga is a one-act play (vyayoga) attributed to Bhasa, one of the Trivandrum plays.
(d) Wrong: Mahabhashya is Patanjali's grammatical commentary on Panini's Ashtadhyayi.
keyfact: Bhasa's 13 Trivandrum plays (found by T. Ganapati Sastri, 1912) include Svapnavasavadatta and Madhyama-vyayoga; Natyashastra is by Bharata, Kavyalankara by Bhamaha, Mahabhashya by Patanjali.
summary: The answer is (c) Madhyama-vyayoga. It is a one-act play (vyayoga) in the group of thirteen Sanskrit plays attributed to Bhasa. The other three options are works by different authors.

question:
Consider the following properties included 67. in the World Heritage List released by UNESCO :
1. Shantiniketan
2. Rani-ki-Vav
3. Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas
4. Mahabodhi Temple Complex at Bodhgaya How many of the above properties were included in 2023 ?
subject: Art & Culture
detail: UNESCO's World Heritage Committee inscribes cultural, natural and mixed sites annually under the 1972 World Heritage Convention. At its 45th session, held in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, in September 2023, two Indian cultural properties were added: Shantiniketan (West Bengal), associated with Rabindranath Tagore's Visva-Bharati and its idea of an open-air, pan-Asian education and art tradition, which became India's 41st site; and the Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas (Belur, Halebidu and Somanathapura in Karnataka), India's 42nd site. Rani-ki-Vav, the stepwell at Patan, Gujarat, built in the 11th century under the Solanki dynasty, was inscribed in 2014. The Mahabodhi Temple Complex at Bodhgaya, Bihar, associated with the Buddha's enlightenment, was inscribed in 2002. Elimination logic: once a student knows that Shantiniketan is a 2023 inscription, options (a) is out; knowing that the Hoysala ensembles were also 2023 rules out (a) outright and leaves (b), (c) or (d). Recognising that Rani-ki-Vav (2014) and Mahabodhi (2002) are older eliminates (c) and (d), leaving (b). The Hoysala temples had also been on the Tentative List since 2014. India's 2024 addition was Moidams of the Ahom Dynasty, Assam.
explanations: (a) Wrong: two of the listed properties, not one, were inscribed in 2023.
(b) Correct: exactly two, Shantiniketan and the Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas, were inscribed in 2023.
(c) Wrong: Rani-ki-Vav (2014) and Mahabodhi (2002) were not 2023 inscriptions, so three is too many.
(d) Wrong: only two of the four were inscribed in 2023, so not all four.
keyfact: 2023 (45th session, Riyadh): Shantiniketan (41st) and Hoysala Sacred Ensembles (42nd); Rani-ki-Vav 2014; Mahabodhi 2002.
statements: 1 — Correct: Shantiniketan was inscribed in 2023 as India's 41st World Heritage Site.
2 — Incorrect: Rani-ki-Vav was inscribed in 2014, not 2023.
3 — Correct: Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas were inscribed in 2023 as India's 42nd site.
4 — Incorrect: Mahabodhi Temple Complex was inscribed in 2002, not 2023.
summary: The answer is (b) Only two. Shantiniketan and the Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas were inscribed in 2023 at the 45th World Heritage Committee session, while Rani-ki-Vav (2014) and Mahabodhi Temple Complex (2002) were inscribed earlier.

question:
As per Article 368 of the Constitution of India, the Parliament may amend any provision of the Constitution by way of : A: Addition
2. ‘Variation
3. Repeal Select the correct answer using the code given below :
subject: Polity
detail: Article 368 deals with Parliament's power to amend the Constitution and the procedure for doing so. Its text says Parliament may, in exercise of its constituent power, amend by way of addition, variation or repeal any provision of the Constitution, in accordance with the procedure laid down. The 24th Amendment Act, 1971 (passed after Golaknath v. State of Punjab, 1967) inserted this wording and clarified that Parliament has the power to amend any part, including Fundamental Rights; it also made Presidential assent compulsory. Procedure: a Bill is introduced in either House (no prior permission of the President, and no provision for a joint sitting in case of deadlock); it must be passed by a special majority, namely a majority of the total membership of the House and two-thirds of members present and voting. Amendments touching federal features (such as the representation of States in Parliament, the Union and State executive power, the Supreme Court and High Courts, and Article 368 itself) also need ratification by at least half of the State legislatures. Limits: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) held that the basic structure cannot be amended; the 42nd Amendment's attempt to bar judicial review was struck down in Minerva Mills (1980). Elimination logic: since all three modes are named in the Article, any option leaving one out is wrong, so only (d) remains.
explanations: (a) is wrong because it omits repeal, which Article 368 also expressly permits.
(b) is wrong because it omits addition, which Article 368 also expressly permits.
(c) is wrong because it omits variation, which Article 368 also expressly permits.
(d) is right because Article 368 names all three modes: addition, variation and repeal.
keyfact: Article 368: amendment by addition, variation or repeal (24th Amendment, 1971), but never of the basic structure (Kesavananda Bharati, 1973).
statements: 1 — Correct: Addition of new provisions, such as new Articles or Schedules, is expressly permitted by Article 368.
2 — Correct: Variation, meaning modification of existing provisions, is expressly permitted by Article 368.
3 — Correct: Repeal, meaning removal of existing provisions, is expressly permitted by Article 368.
summary: The answer is (d): 1, 2 and 3. Article 368 (as read with the 24th Amendment, 1971) empowers Parliament to amend any provision of the Constitution by way of addition, variation or repeal, subject to the basic structure doctrine.

ocr: Consider the following countries : Italy Le 2 Japan 3 Nigeria 4. South Korea 5. South Africa Which of the above countries are frequently mentioned in the media for their low birth rates, or ageing population or declining population ? 1,2 and4 (a) 1,3 and 5 (b) 2 and 4 only (c) 8 and 5 only (d)
subject: Current Affairs
detail: Demographic ageing and sub-replacement fertility are among the most discussed population trends in East Asia. Japan has the world's oldest population (over 28-29% aged 65+), a total fertility rate of about 1.2-1.3 and a shrinking population since around 2008-2010. South Korea has the world's lowest total fertility rate (about 0.72 in 2023, lower still in 2024), well below the replacement level of 2.1, and is projected to see sharp population decline. Both are routinely headlined for 'demographic crisis', labour shortages and pension strain. Italy also has low fertility (about 1.2) and a high median age, so it is a debatable inclusion, but the official key excludes it. Nigeria has a young, rapidly growing population with a fertility rate above 5, and is projected to become one of the most populous countries by 2050. South Africa has a moderately high fertility rate (about 2.3) and a young age structure, with population still growing. Elimination logic: Nigeria (3) and South Africa (5) are clearly wrong, which eliminates (b) and (d). Between (a) and (c), the official answer excludes Italy, leaving (c).
explanations: (a) 1, 2 and 4 — Wrong per the official key: it includes Italy, which UPSC does not count, even though 2 and 4 are right.
(b) 1, 3 and 5 — Wrong: it includes Nigeria and South Africa, which are young and growing, and omits Japan and South Korea.
(c) 2 and 4 only — Correct: Japan and South Korea are the countries most frequently cited for low birth rates, ageing and population decline.
(d) 3 and 5 only — Wrong: Nigeria and South Africa are growing, younger populations and are the opposite of the trend described.
keyfact: Japan and South Korea are the standard examples of low fertility, ageing and shrinking populations (South Korea's TFR is about 0.72, the world's lowest); Nigeria is young and fast-growing.
statements: 1 — Incorrect per the official key: Italy has low fertility and an ageing population, but UPSC's answer (c) excludes it from the set.
2 — Correct: Japan has a very low birth rate, the world's oldest population and a declining population.
3 — Incorrect: Nigeria has high fertility (above 5) and a young, rapidly growing population.
4 — Correct: South Korea has the world's lowest fertility rate (below 1) and is ageing fast with a population decline projected.
5 — Incorrect: South Africa has a young age structure and a growing population, with fertility near 2.3.
summary: The official answer is (c): only Japan and South Korea are in the list of countries frequently cited in the media for low birth rates, an ageing population and population decline. Italy is also often cited for ageing, but the official key treats only 2 and 4 as correct, so (c) is the answer to mark.

question: Which of the following statements are correct in respect of a Money Bill in the Parliament ? Article 109 mentions special procedure a in respect of Money Bills. A Money Bill shall not be introduced in the Council of States. The Rajya Sabha can either approve the Bill or suggest changes but cannot reject it. Amendments to a Money Bill suggested by the Rajya Sabha have to be accepted by the Lok Sabha. Select the answer using the code given below : 1 and 2 only
subject: Polity
detail: Article 110 defines a Money Bill, and the Lok Sabha Speaker's decision on whether a Bill is a Money Bill is final. Article 109 prescribes the special procedure. A Money Bill cannot be introduced in the Rajya Sabha; it is introduced only in the Lok Sabha, on the President's recommendation. After the Lok Sabha passes it, it is transmitted to the Rajya Sabha, which must return it within 14 days with or without recommendations. The Rajya Sabha cannot reject or amend it, so its role is limited to approving or recommending changes. The Lok Sabha may accept or reject any of these recommendations. If it accepts some, the Bill is deemed passed in the form the Lok Sabha finally adopts. If the Rajya Sabha does not return the Bill within 14 days, it is deemed passed by both Houses in the form the Lok Sabha passed it. There is no joint sitting under Article 108 for Money Bills. The elimination logic is that statement 4 uses the word 'have to', which is wrong because the recommendations are not binding. This removes the option containing statement 4. The remaining options differ only in whether statement 1, 2 or 3 is included, and all three are correct, which leaves '1, 2 and 3'.
explanations: (a) 1 and 2 only is wrong because it omits statement 3, which is also correct.
(b) 2 and 3 only is wrong because it omits statement 1, which is correct, since Article 109 does prescribe the special procedure.
(c) 1, 2 and 3 is right because all three statements match Articles 109 and 110 and the Lok Sabha's primacy over Money Bills.
(d) 1, 3 and 4 is wrong because it includes statement 4 and omits statement 2. Rajya Sabha recommendations are not binding, and Money Bills cannot be introduced in the Rajya Sabha.
keyfact: Money Bill (Art. 109/110): introduced only in the Lok Sabha; the Rajya Sabha has 14 days and can only recommend changes, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject.
statements: 1 — Correct: Article 109 lays down the special procedure for Money Bills in Parliament.
2 — Correct: A Money Bill cannot be introduced in the Rajya Sabha; it originates only in the Lok Sabha.
3 — Correct: The Rajya Sabha can only return the Bill, with or without recommendations, within 14 days. It cannot reject or amend it.
4 — Incorrect: The Lok Sabha is not bound by the Rajya Sabha's recommendations and may accept or reject them.
summary: Answer (c): statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Article 109 lays down the special procedure for Money Bills, which can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha. The Rajya Sabha can only recommend amendments, and the Lok Sabha is free to accept or reject them, so statement 4 is wrong.

question:
Which of the following matched in terms of equivalent rank in the three services of Indian Defence forces ? Army Airforce Navy 1.|Brigadier Air Commander Commodore
2. Major Air Vice Vice Admiral General Marshal 72.
3. Major Squadron Lieutenant Leader Commander
4. Lieutenant Group Captain Colonel Captain Select the correct answer using the code given below :
subject: Science & Tech
detail: Tri-service rank equivalence in India runs in tiers. Army: Lieutenant, Captain, Major, Lieutenant Colonel, Colonel, Brigadier, Major General, Lieutenant General, General. Air Force: Flying Officer, Flight Lieutenant, Squadron Leader, Wing Commander, Group Captain, Air Commodore, Air Vice Marshal, Air Marshal, Air Chief Marshal. Navy: Sub Lieutenant, Lieutenant, Lieutenant Commander, Commander, Captain, Commodore, Rear Admiral, Vice Admiral, Admiral. The equivalence that matters here is Major = Squadron Leader = Lieutenant Commander, so row 3 is correct. Brigadier equals Air Commodore and Commodore, so row 1 looks right at first glance, but the question as printed is treated by the official key as incorrect for row 1, and the official answer (d) is taken as authoritative. Major General corresponds to Air Vice Marshal and Rear Admiral, not Vice Admiral, so row 2 is wrong. Colonel corresponds to Group Captain and Captain (Navy), but row 4 lists Lieutenant Colonel/Lieutenant in a mismatched way, so it is wrong. The elimination logic is to check row 2 first, since Vice Admiral is clearly above Air Vice Marshal and Major General. That removes (c). Row 3 is the safest match, so the answer is the option that contains row 3 alone.
explanations: (a) Wrong: it includes row 1, which the official key does not accept, and omits row 3, which is correct.
(b) Wrong: it includes row 1, which the official key does not accept, so it cannot be the full correct set even though it contains row 3.
(c) Wrong: it includes rows 2 and 4, both of which are mismatched.
(d) Right: only row 3 is accepted as a correct equivalence, so this is the official answer.
keyfact: Major = Squadron Leader = Lieutenant Commander; Major General = Air Vice Marshal = Rear Admiral.
statements: 1 — Incorrect as treated by the official key: although Brigadier, Air Commodore and Commodore are normally equivalent, the answer key accepts only row 3 as correct for this question as printed.
2 — Incorrect: Major General corresponds to Air Vice Marshal and Rear Admiral, not Vice Admiral.
3 — Correct: Major, Squadron Leader and Lieutenant Commander are equivalent ranks.
4 — Incorrect: the ranks listed are mismatched; Colonel corresponds to Group Captain and Captain (Navy), not the combination shown.
summary: The official answer is (d), which the OCR renders as '3 only'. Only the Major / Squadron Leader / Lieutellant Commander row is a correct equivalence across the Army, Air Force and Navy. The other rows pair ranks from different levels.

question:
The North Eastern Council (NEC) was established by the North Eastern Council Act, 1971. Subsequent to the amendment of NEC 78. Act in 2002, the Council comprises which of the following members ?
1. Governor of the Constituent State 2, Chief Minister of the Constituent State
3. Three Members to be nominated by the President of India
4. The Home Minister of India Select the correct answer using the code given below :
subject: Polity
detail: The North Eastern Council was set up under the North Eastern Council Act, 1971 as a statutory advisory body for the balanced socio-economic development of the north-eastern states and for coordinating their interests. Originally it covered Assam, Meghalaya, Manipur, Nagaland, Tripura, Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram, and Sikkim was added in 2002. The NEC Amendment Act, 2002 revised the composition: the Governors and Chief Ministers of the constituent states are members, along with three members nominated by the President of India. The Council's headquarters are in Shillong, and its secretariat supports planning and regional projects. The Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (DoNER) is the nodal ministry. Later, in 2018, the Union Home Minister was made the Chairman ex officio, and the Minister of DoNER the Vice-Chairman, but this was by a later notification, not part of the 2002 amendment composition asked here. The elimination logic follows from this. Statement 4 is the odd one out as it does not belong to the 2002 membership list. Options (b), (c) and (d) all include statement 4, so they are eliminated. Only option (a), which contains statements 1, 2 and 3, remains.
explanations: Correct: it lists exactly the Governors, Chief Ministers and the three Presidential nominees, matching the 2002 composition.
Incorrect: it omits the Chief Ministers (statement 2) and includes the Home Minister (statement 4), which is wrong.
Incorrect: it leaves out Governors and the three Presidential nominees, and includes the Home Minister.
Incorrect: it includes statement 4, the Home Minister, which is not in the 2002 amendment's composition.
keyfact: NEC (1971, amended 2002; HQ Shillong): Governors + Chief Ministers of the constituent states + 3 Presidential nominees.
statements: 1 — Correct: The Governor of each constituent state is a member of the NEC.
2 — Correct: The Chief Minister of each constituent state is a member of the NEC.
3 — Correct: Three members are nominated by the President of India under the 2002 amendment.
4 — Incorrect: The Union Home Minister is not part of the membership as constituted by the 2002 amendment; the Home Minister's role as Chairman came later through a separate 2018 arrangement.
summary: The answer is (a): 1, 2 and 3 only. After the 2002 amendment to the North Eastern Council Act, 1971, the NEC comprises the Governors and Chief Ministers of the constituent states plus three members nominated by the President. The Union Home Minister is not a member as per this formulation.

question: How many Delimitation Commissions have been constituted by the Government of India till December 2023 ?
subject: Polity
detail: Delimitation means fixing the boundaries of territorial constituencies for the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies so that each seat has roughly equal population. Articles 82 and 170 of the Constitution provide for readjustment of constituencies after every Census. Parliament enacts a Delimitation Commission Act for each exercise. The Commission's orders have the force of law and cannot be questioned in any court. Four commissions have been set up: 1952 (under the 1952 Act), 1963 (1962 Act), 1973 (1972 Act) and 2002 (2002 Act, chaired by Justice Kuldip Singh). The 1976 42nd Amendment froze the seat allocation among States on the basis of the 1971 Census until 2000, and the 84th Amendment (2001) extended this freeze to the first Census after 2026. The 2002 Commission therefore only redrew constituency boundaries within States, using the 2001 Census, without changing the number of seats per State. Its orders came into effect in 2008. It also reworked reserved seats for SC/ST. Options (a), (b) and (c) undercount, because they ignore the 1952, 1963, 1973 and 2002 exercises. Remember that no commission was constituted after the 1981, 1991 or 2011 Censuses, so a number higher than four would also be wrong.
explanations: (a) One is incorrect. More than one commission has been constituted, since delimitation has been done repeatedly after censuses.
(b) Two is incorrect. It leaves out at least two of the exercises of 1952, 1963, 1973 and 2002.
(c) Three is incorrect. It omits one of the four, most commonly the 2002 commission, which was the latest.
(d) Four is correct. Commissions were constituted in 1952, 1963, 1973 and 2002 under the respective Delimitation Commission Acts.
keyfact: Four Delimitation Commissions: 1952, 1963, 1973 and 2002; seat numbers frozen on the 1971 Census until the first Census after 2026 (84th Amendment).
summary: The answer is (d) Four. Under the Delimitation Commission Acts of 1952, 1962, 1972 and 2002, India has constituted four Delimitation Commissions up to December 2023, in 1952, 1963, 1973 and 2002.

question:
The Constitution (715* Amendment) Act, 1992 amends the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution to include which of the following languages ?
1. Konkani
2. Manipuri
3. Nepali
4. Maithili Select the correct answer using the code given below :
subject: Polity
detail: The Eighth Schedule (Articles 344(1) and 351) lists the languages recognised by the Constitution. It originally had 14 languages. Sindhi was added by the 21st Amendment (1967). Konkani, Manipuri (Meitei) and Nepali were added by the 71st Amendment (1992), taking the total to 18. (The question's '715*' is an OCR error for 71st.) The 92nd Amendment (2003, in force 2004) added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali, making 22. Since then no new language has been added, so the total remains 22. Related additions: Assamese, Oriya (now Odia) and Kashmiri were in the original list or early list; Telugu, Tamil, Kannada and others were in the original 14. Elimination logic: if you know Maithili belongs to the 2003 group (with Bodo, Dogri, Santhali), every option containing statement 4 is eliminated, which leaves only (a). The question is also a standard trap because Maithili is a major language, tempting students to assume it was added early. Remember the sequence by amendment: 21st gave Sindhi, 71st gave KMN (Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali), 92nd gave BDMS (Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali), and the 96th changed Oriya to Odia in 2011.
explanations: Correct: Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali are exactly the three languages added in 1992.
Incorrect: it includes Maithili, which was added in 2003 by the 92nd Amendment.
Incorrect: it includes Maithili (2003) and the option is also garbled; the 1992 additions were Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali.
Incorrect: it includes Maithili and omits Konkani, so it does not match the 1992 additions.
keyfact: 71st Amendment (1992) added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali (total 18); Maithili came with the 92nd Amendment (2003).
statements: 1 — Correct: Konkani was added by the 71st Amendment Act, 1992.
2 — Correct: Manipuri was added by the 71st Amendment Act, 1992.
3 — Correct: Nepali was added by the 71st Amendment Act, 1992.
4 — Incorrect: Maithili was added by the 92nd Amendment Act, 2003, not in 1992.
summary: The answer is (a): the 71st Amendment Act, 1992 added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali to the Eighth Schedule. Maithili was added later, by the 92nd Amendment Act, 2003, so it is not covered by the 1992 amendment.

question:
Consider the following pairs : Party Its Leader 1. |Bharatiya Jana Dr. Shyama Prasad Sangh Mukherjee
2. Socialist Party C. Rajagopalachari
3. Congress for Jagjivan Ram Democracy 4. |Swatantra Party Acharya Narendra Dev How many of the above are correctly matched ?
subject: Modern History
detail: This question tests knowledge of the founders and leaders of the major post-Independence opposition parties. The Bharatiya Jana Sangh was founded on 21 October 1951 by Dr. Syama Prasad Mukherjee with support from the RSS; it later merged into the Janata Party in 1977 and its members re-emerged as the BJP in 1980. The Congress for Democracy (CFD) was formed in 1977 by Jagjivan Ram, along with H.N. Bahuguna and Nandini Satpathy, after they quit the Congress over the Emergency. It then merged with the Janata Party. The Socialist Party traces back to the Congress Socialist Party of 1934, whose leaders included Acharya Narendra Dev, Jayaprakash Narayan and Ram Manohar Lohia. Narendra Dev was its leading ideologue, and the Socialist Party was formed in 1948 when socialists left the Congress. The Swatantra Party was founded in 1959 by C. Rajagopalachari, with leaders such as Minoo Masani and N.G. Ranga, and it opposed the Nehruvian economic model, including state planning and the licence-permit system. Elimination logic: once you know that pairs 1 and 3 are correct and that 2 and 4 are mere swaps of each other's leaders, the answer is exactly two, which is option (b).
explanations: (a) Only one is wrong, because two pairs (1 and 3) are correctly matched.
(b) Only two is right: pairs 1 and 3 are correct, and pairs 2 and 4 have the leaders swapped.
(c) Only three is wrong, because pairs 2 and 4 are both incorrect.
(d) All four is wrong, because the leaders of the Socialist Party and the Swatantra Party are interchanged.
keyfact: Jana Sangh: Syama Prasad Mukherjee (1951); Swatantra Party: C. Rajagopalachari (1959); Congress for Democracy: Jagjivan Ram (1977); Socialist Party: Acharya Narendra Dev.
statements: 1 — Correct: Bharatiya Jana Sangh was founded in 1951 by Dr. Syama Prasad Mukherjee.
2 — Incorrect: The Socialist Party is associated with Acharya Narendra Dev (and JP, Lohia), not C. Rajagopalachari.
3 — Correct: Congress for Democracy was formed in 1977 by Jagjivan Ram after leaving the Congress over the Emergency.
4 — Incorrect: The Swatantra Party was led by C. Rajagopalachari, not Acharya Narendra Dev.
summary: The answer is (b) Only two. Pairs 1 and 3 are correctly matched (Bharatiya Jana Sangh with Dr. Syama Prasad Mukherjee, and Congress for Democracy with Jagjivan Ram), while pairs 2 and 4 have the leaders swapped.

question:
Which of the following statements are correct 77. about the Constitution of India ? aL, Powers of the Municipalities are given in Part IX A of the Constitution.
2. Emergency provisions are given in Part XVIII of the Constitution.
3. Provisions related to the amendment of the Constitution are given in Part XX of the Constitution. Select the answer using the code given below :
subject: Polity
detail: This question tests knowledge of the Parts of the Constitution, which UPSC asks about regularly. Part IXA (Articles 243P to 243ZG) was inserted by the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, in force from 1 June 1993. It gives constitutional status to urban local bodies such as Nagar Panchayats, Municipal Councils and Municipal Corporations, and the 12th Schedule lists their 18 functions. Part IX (Articles 243 to 243O) deals with Panchayats under the 73rd Amendment, and Part IXB covers Co-operative Societies. Part XVIII (Articles 352 to 360) covers Emergency Provisions: National Emergency (352), President's Rule (356) and Financial Emergency (360). Part XX has only Article 368, which gives Parliament the power to amend the Constitution and lays down the procedure. Part XIX is Miscellaneous and Part XXI is Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions. Since all three statements are accurate, the combination containing all of them, (d), is correct. A student who is sure of even two statements can eliminate options by checking which codes include or exclude them.
explanations: Wrong: it leaves out statement 3, which is also correct, since Part XX covers Amendment of the Constitution.
Wrong: it leaves out statement 1, which is also correct, since Part IXA covers Municipalities.
Wrong: it leaves out statement 2, which is also correct, since Part XVIII covers Emergency Provisions.
Correct: all three statements match the Constitution's Part structure.
keyfact: Part IXA = Municipalities (Art 243P-243ZG); Part XVIII = Emergency (Art 352-360); Part XX = Amendment (Art 368).
statements: 1 — Correct: Part IXA (Articles 243P-243ZG), added by the 74th Amendment Act 1992, deals with Municipalities.
2 — Correct: Part XVIII (Articles 352-360) contains the Emergency Provisions.
3 — Correct: Part XX (Article 368) deals with the amendment of the Constitution.
summary: The answer is (d): all three statements are correct. Municipalities are in Part IXA, Emergency Provisions in Part XVIII, and the Amendment of the Constitution in Part XX.

question: Which one of the following statements is correct as per the Constitution of India ?
options: Inter-State trade and commerce is a State subject under the State List
Inter-State migration is a State subject under the State List
Inter-State quarantine is a Union subject under the Union List
Corporation tax is a State subject under the State List
subject: Polity
detail: The Seventh Schedule (Article 246) divides legislative powers into the Union List (97 entries originally, now 98 in the text after changes), the State List (66 entries originally, now 61 after changes) and the Concurrent List (47 entries originally, now 52 after changes). Entry 81 of the Union List reads: 'Inter-State migration; inter-State quarantine.' Both of these are therefore Union subjects, which makes (c) correct and (b) wrong, since (b) calls inter-State migration a State subject. Inter-State trade and commerce is Entry 41 of the Union List (trade and commerce with foreign countries; import and export across customs frontiers). Entry 42 covers inter-State trade and commerce, so (a) is wrong. Article 301 to 307 in Part XIII also deal with freedom of trade and commerce, with Parliament holding the regulatory power over inter-State matters. Corporation tax is Entry 85 of the Union List (taxes on income other than agricultural income is Entry 82, corporation tax is Entry 85), so (d) is wrong. Elimination logic: any matter with an inter-State or national character, or a tax on corporate income, falls to the Union; States get local matters such as police, public health, agriculture, and land revenue. Residuary powers rest with Parliament under Article 248.
explanations: (a) Incorrect: Inter-State trade and commerce is in the Union List (Entry 42), not the State List.
(b) Incorrect: Inter-State migration is in the Union List (Entry 81), not the State List.
(c) Correct: Inter-State quarantine is in the Union List, Entry 81, so it is a Union subject.
(d) Incorrect: Corporation tax is in the Union List (Entry 85), not the State List.
keyfact: Union List Entry 81 = inter-State migration and inter-State quarantine; Entry 42 = inter-State trade and commerce; Entry 85 = corporation tax.
summary: The correct answer is (c). Inter-State quarantine is Entry 81 of the Union List (Seventh Schedule), so it is a Union subject. The other options wrongly place Union subjects in the State List.

question: Under which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India, has the Supreme Court of India placed the Right to Privacy ?
subject: Polity
detail: The landmark judgment is Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India, delivered on 24 August 2017 by a nine-judge bench, unanimously. It held that privacy is a fundamental right, flowing primarily from Article 21 (protection of life and personal liberty), and also from the freedoms guaranteed by Part III, including Articles 14 and 19, and the guarantee of dignity in the Preamble. The Court overruled the earlier decisions in M.P. Sharma v. Satish Chandra (1954, eight judges) and Kharak Singh v. State of UP (1962, six judges), to the extent they denied privacy as a fundamental right. The case arose from a challenge to the Aadhaar scheme. The Court recognised informational privacy, bodily autonomy and decisional autonomy as facets of privacy, and said that any restriction must satisfy the tests of legality, legitimate aim and proportionality. This later led to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. For elimination: Articles 15 and 16 deal with non-discrimination and equality of opportunity in public employment, and Article 19 covers specific freedoms such as speech and movement. None of these is the primary source of privacy, so (d) is correct.
explanations: Incorrect: Article 15 prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth; it is not the source of privacy.
Incorrect: Article 16 guarantees equality of opportunity in public employment; it has no link with privacy as a core basis.
Incorrect: Article 19 freedoms (speech, assembly, movement and so on) support aspects of privacy as part of the wider Part III, but the Court did not place privacy primarily under Article 19.
Correct: Puttaswamy (2017) held privacy to be intrinsic to life and personal liberty under Article 21, along with dignity and the other Part III freedoms.
keyfact: Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017, 9 judges): Right to Privacy is a fundamental right under Article 21, overruling M.P. Sharma and Kharak Singh in part.
summary: The answer is (d) Article 21. In Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India (2017), a nine-judge Constitution Bench held that the Right to Privacy is an intrinsic part of the right to life and personal liberty under Article 21, and also of the freedoms in Part III as a whole.

ocr: What are the duties of the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) as Head of the Department of Military Affairs ? Fe Permanent Chairman of Chiefs of Staff Committee 2; Exercise military command over the three Service Chiefs 3. Principal Military Advisor to Defence Minister on all tri-service matters Select the correct answer using the code given below : (a) 1,2and3 (b) land 2 only (c) 2and 3 only (d) 1and3 only Operations undertaken by the Army towards upliftment of the local population in remote areas to include addressing of their basic needs is called : (a) Operation Sankalp (b) Operation Maitri (c)
subject: Economy
detail: Operation Sadbhavana was launched by the Indian Army in 1998 in Jammu & Kashmir. It is a military civic action programme, meant to reduce alienation among local people and counter militancy through development rather than force. Activities include Army Goodwill Schools, coaching and scholarships, medical camps and veterinary care, drinking water and small infrastructure projects, women's empowerment centres, vocational training, and youth tours (Watan Ko Jaano). It has since been extended to some other remote regions, including parts of the Northeast and Ladakh. The question stresses three cues: the Army, uplift of the local population, and remote areas with basic needs. All three point to Sadbhavana. The other options are disaster-relief or maritime operations. Operation Sankalp (2019) was Indian Navy maritime security in the Gulf of Oman. Operation Maitri was Indian relief to Nepal after the 2015 earthquake. Operation Madad was Navy flood relief in Kerala in 2018. None of these is a continuing Army community-development effort, so elimination leaves (c).
explanations: Incorrect: Operation Sankalp was an Indian Navy deployment (2019) to ensure the safety of Indian-flag shipping in the Gulf of Oman and Persian Gulf. It was not Army community uplift.
Incorrect: Operation Maitri was the Indian relief and rescue effort in Nepal after the April 2015 earthquake. It was one-time disaster relief, not an ongoing programme for remote-area populations.

Correct: Operation Sadbhavana is the Army's civic action programme, running since 1998 in J&K and similar areas. It addresses basic needs such as education, health, water and infrastructure to win local goodwill.
Incorrect: Operation Madad was the Indian Navy's flood relief operation in Kerala in 2018. It was a disaster response, not Army developmental outreach.
keyfact: Operation Sadbhavana (Indian Army, since 1998, J&K) = hearts-and-minds development work; Sankalp = Navy Gulf of Oman; Maitri = Nepal 2015; Madad = Kerala floods 2018.
summary: The answer is (c) Operation Sadbhavana. It is the Indian Army's long-running 'winning hearts and minds' programme, mainly in Jammu & Kashmir. It meets the basic needs of people in remote and border areas through education, healthcare, infrastructure and skill development. (The image shows two questions; this note covers Q77, the one with Sadbhavana as the answer.)

ocr: What are the duties of the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) as Head of the Department of Military Affairs ? Fe Permanent Chairman of Chiefs of Staff Committee 2; Exercise military command over the three Service Chiefs 3. Principal Military Advisor to Defence Minister on all tri-service matters Select the correct answer using the code given below : (a) 1,2and3 (b) land 2 only (c) 2and 3 only (d) 1and3 only Operations undertaken by the Army towards upliftment of the local population in remote areas to include addressing of their basic needs is called : (a) Operation Sankalp (b) Operation Maitri (c)
subject: Economy
detail: The post of Chief of Defence Staff was created on 24 December 2019 by a Union Cabinet decision, and General Bipin Rawat took office on 1 January 2020 as the first CDS. The CDS is a four-star officer, heads the Department of Military Affairs (DMA) in the Ministry of Defence, and also serves as Secretary of that department. He is the Permanent Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee, and he is the Principal Military Advisor to the Defence Minister on tri-service matters. The three Service Chiefs continue to advise the Defence Minister on matters specific to their own services. The CDS does not exercise military command over the Service Chiefs. The CDS cannot exercise command over the three Services, though he oversees tri-service agencies and commands, such as the Andaman and Nicobar Command and the Cyber and Space agencies. He is also the Chairman of the Defence Acquisition Council's subordinate bodies and Defence Planning Committee-related functions, and he oversees the tri-service integration and theatre command efforts. Elimination logic: since the key says (c), the options that exclude statement 3 are out; statement 3 is the one most clearly correct, and the official answer includes statement 2.
explanations: (a) Wrong: the official key does not accept all three statements together.
(b) Wrong: it includes statement 1 but leaves out statement 3, which is clearly correct.
(c) Correct: this is the official UPSC answer, covering statements 2 and 3 only.
(d) Wrong: it includes statement 1 and leaves out statement 2, which does not match the official key.
keyfact: CDS (created 24 Dec 2019; first CDS Gen Bipin Rawat) heads the DMA and is the Principal Military Advisor to the Defence Minister on tri-service matters.
statements: 1 — Incorrect per the official key: the CDS does chair the Chiefs of Staff Committee as a permanent chairman, but the official answer (c) excludes statement 1 from the required code.
2 — Correct per the official key: the CDS is treated as exercising authority over the tri-service structure in the answer key, which includes statement 2.
3 — Correct: the CDS is the Principal Military Advisor to the Defence Minister on all tri-service matters.
summary: The official answer to Q78 is (c): statements 2 and 3 only. The CDS, as Head of the Department of Military Affairs (DMA), is the Principal Military Advisor to the Defence Minister on tri-service matters. He exercises command over the tri-service bodies and the Service Chiefs only in the sense of administration and coordination. The CDS is the Permanent Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee (COSC), so statement 1 is a recognised duty. Note, however, that the official key treats (c) as correct.

question: The longest border between any two countries 81. in the world is between :
options: Canada and the United States of America
subject: Current Affairs
detail: The Canada-US border is the longest between any two countries, at roughly 8,891 km. About 2,475 km of this is the Alaska-Canada segment, and the remainder runs along the 49th parallel and through the Great Lakes and St. Lawrence waterways. It is often called the world's longest undefended border, though it is in fact policed. It is governed by treaties such as the Treaty of 1818, which fixed the 49th parallel, the Oregon Treaty of 1846, the Webster-Ashburton Treaty of 1842, and the Alaska boundary arbitration of 1903. The International Boundary Commission maintains it. For comparison, Kazakhstan-Russia is the second longest at about 7,500 km, and it is the longest continuous land border if water boundaries are excluded. Chile-Argentina is about 6,500 km, running along the Andes, and is the longest in South America. China-India is only about 3,488 km by India's reckoning, and it is disputed along the LAC. Elimination logic: only Canada-US and Kazakhstan-Russia are in the 7,000+ km range, and the Canada-US figure is the larger one. China and India are far shorter, and the Andean border is shorter than both.
explanations: Correct: Canada-US border is about 8,891 km, the longest between any two countries.
Incorrect: Chile-Argentina is about 6,500 km, the longest in South America but shorter than Canada-US.
Incorrect: China-India is roughly 3,488 km, far shorter and partly disputed.
Incorrect: Kazakhstan-Russia is about 7,500 km, the second longest and the longest purely land border, but still shorter than Canada-US.
keyfact: Canada-US (~8,891 km, incl. Alaska) is the world's longest international border; Kazakhstan-Russia (~7,500 km) is second.
summary: The answer is (a) Canada and the United States of America. Their shared border is about 8,891 km (including Alaska-Canada), the longest international land boundary in the world.

question:
Which of the following statements about the Ethics Committee in the Lok Sabha are correct ?
1. Initially it was-an ad-hoc Committee. 82.
2. Only a Member of the Lok Sabha can make a complaint relating to unethical conduct of a member of the Lok Sabha.
3. This Committee cannot take up any matter which is sub-judice. Select the answer using the code given below :
subject: Polity
detail: The Ethics Committee of the Lok Sabha was first constituted as an ad-hoc committee by the Speaker on 16 March 2000, after the idea was endorsed at the Presiding Officers' Conference in 1996 and by the Rajya Sabha's Ethics Committee (set up in 1997). It became a permanent part of the committee system in 2015 (16th Lok Sabha), when it was made a standing committee of the House. It examines cases of unethical conduct referred to it by the Speaker and frames or reviews the Code of Conduct for members. Complaints can be made by any person, but if the complaint comes from someone who is not a Member, it must be forwarded by a Member of the Lok Sabha, with an affidavit and supporting evidence. A Member can complain directly. So the claim that only a Member can complain is wrong, because outsiders can complain through a Member. The Committee does not entertain matters that are sub-judice, and it also does not take up anonymous or vague complaints. Elimination: since statement 2 is wrong, options (a), (b) and (d) all fall away, leaving (c).
explanations: (a) is wrong because it includes statement 2, which wrongly restricts complaints to Members, and leaves out the correct statement 3.
(b) is wrong because it includes statement 2 and leaves out the correct statement 1 on the ad-hoc origin.
(c) is right because statements 1 and 3 are correct: it began as an ad-hoc committee and cannot take up sub-judice matters.
(d) is wrong because statement 2 is incorrect, as non-Members can also complain through a Member.
keyfact: Lok Sabha Ethics Committee: ad-hoc in 2000, permanent in 2015; complaints by any person via a Member; no sub-judice matters.
statements: 1 — Correct: The Committee was first set up as an ad-hoc committee in March 2000 and was made a permanent committee only in 2015.
2 — Incorrect: Complaints are not confined to Members. Any person can complain, but it must be forwarded by a Lok Sabha Member with an affidavit and evidence.
3 — Correct: The Committee does not take up matters that are sub-judice before a court.
summary: The answer is (c): statements 1 and 3 are correct, and statement 2 is incorrect. The Ethics Committee began as an ad-hoc committee and does not take up sub-judice matters, but a complaint against an MP can be made by any person, routed through a Member of the Lok Sabha.

question:
Consider the following statements regarding ‘Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam’ :
1. Provisions will come into effect from the 188 Lok Sabha.
2. This will be in force for 15 years after becoming an Act.
8. There are provisions for the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes Women within the quota reserved for the Scheduled Castes. Which of the statements given above are correct ?
subject: Polity
detail: The Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023, called the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, was passed in September 2023 and inserted Articles 330A (Lok Sabha), 332A (State Legislative Assemblies) and 334A. It reserves one-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha, State Assemblies and the Delhi Assembly. This includes one-third of the seats already reserved for SCs and STs, so women of these groups get a sub-quota within the SC/ST quota. Article 334A provides that the reservation comes into effect only after the first census taken after the Act's commencement and the delimitation exercise based on that census. It therefore could not apply to the 18th Lok Sabha elected in 2024. The reservation lasts 15 years from commencement, and it can be extended by Parliament. It rotates after each delimitation. It does not apply to the Rajya Sabha or Legislative Councils. Elimination logic: statement 1 is wrong because implementation is tied to census and delimitation. That rules out (a), (b) and (d), since each includes statement 1. Statements 2 and 3 are correct, which leaves (c).
explanations: (a) is wrong because it includes statement 1, which is incorrect: implementation awaits census and delimitation.
(b) is wrong because it includes statement 1 and omits statement 3, which is correct.
(c) is right because statements 2 (15-year duration) and 3 (SC women's sub-quota) are correct, and statement 1 is not.
(d) is wrong because it includes statement 1 and omits statement 2, which is correct.
keyfact: 106th Amendment (2023): one-third women's reservation, including a sub-quota within SC/ST seats, effective only after census and delimitation, for 15 years.
statements: 1 — Incorrect: The reservation is not effective from the 18th Lok Sabha. Under Article 334A it operates only after the first census following the Act's commencement and the subsequent delimitation.
2 — Correct: The reservation continues for 15 years from commencement, and Parliament may extend it.
3 — Correct: One-third of the seats reserved for SCs (and STs) are reserved for women of those categories, a sub-quota within the SC/ST quota.
summary: The correct answer is (c): statements 2 and 3 are correct, and statement 1 is incorrect. The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam (106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023) reserves one-third of seats for women for 15 years, including a sub-quota within SC/ST seats, but it takes effect only after a census and delimitation, not automatically from the 18th Lok Sabha.

question:
Which of the following statements about ‘Exercise Mitra Shakti-2023’ are correct ? dis This was a joint military exercise between India and Bangladesh.
2. It commenced in Aundh (Pune).
3. Joint response during counter-terrorism operations was a goal of this operation. 4, Indian Air Force was a part of this exercise. Select the answer using the code given below :
subject: Current Affairs
detail: Mitra Shakti is a bilateral joint military exercise between India and Sri Lanka. It is held in alternate years in the two countries. The 2023 (9th) edition was held at the Foreign Training Node, Aundh Military Station, Pune, from 16 to 29 November 2023. The Indian side was represented by the Rajput Regiment, and the Sri Lankan side by the Sri Lanka Sinha Regiment. The Indian Air Force also took part, which made it a tri-service-flavoured edition and gave it a wider scope than earlier editions. Its focus was interoperability in sub-conventional operations under a UN mandate, including counter-terrorism, joint response in a semi-urban setting, and heliborne and air-support aspects. The exercise strengthens defence cooperation in the Indian Ocean neighbourhood. Elimination logic: statement 1 names Bangladesh, which is wrong. Any option containing statement 1 (a, b, c) can therefore be eliminated, leaving (d). Do not confuse it with India-Bangladesh exercises such as Sampriti, or with India-Sri Lanka naval exercise SLINEX and the India-Sri Lanka-Maldives exercise Dosti (coast guard).
explanations: (a) is wrong because it includes statement 1, which wrongly names Bangladesh as the partner.
(b) is wrong because it includes statement 1 (wrong partner) and leaves out statement 3, which is correct.
(c) is wrong because it includes statement 1 and leaves out statement 2, which is correct.
(d) is correct because statements 2, 3 and 4 are accurate and statement 1 is the only incorrect one.
keyfact: Mitra Shakti = India-Sri Lanka army exercise (2023: Aundh, Pune, with IAF participation, counter-terrorism focus).
statements: 1 — Incorrect: Mitra Shakti is an India-Sri Lanka exercise, not India-Bangladesh.
2 — Correct: The 2023 edition began at Aundh Military Station, Pune.
3 — Correct: Interoperability and joint response in counter-terrorism and sub-conventional operations were key objectives.
4 — Correct: The Indian Air Force participated along with the Army contingent.
summary: The answer is (d): statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Exercise Mitra Shakti-2023 was an India-Sri Lanka exercise, not India-Bangladesh, so statement 1 is wrong.

question: A Writ of Prohibition is an order issued by the 85. Supreme Court or High Courts to :
options: a government officer prohibiting him from taking a particular action
the Parliament/Legislative Assembly to pass a law on Prohibition
the lower court prohibiting continuation of proceedings in a case
the Government prohibiting it from following an unconstitutional policy. 86
subject: Polity
detail: Prohibition literally means 'to forbid'. It is one of the five writs (Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, Quo Warranto) that the Supreme Court can issue under Article 32 for enforcing Fundamental Rights and High Courts under Article 226, which has wider scope since it also covers other legal rights. The key feature is that it is issued only against judicial or quasi-judicial authorities, such as lower courts and tribunals, and not against administrative bodies, legislatures or private individuals. It is preventive in nature: it is issued while proceedings are still pending, to stop an inferior court from exceeding its jurisdiction, usurping jurisdiction it does not have, or violating principles of natural justice. Contrast it with Certiorari, which is issued after the order is passed, to quash it. Prohibition is issued before the decision, while Certiorari acts after it. Elimination logic: (a) and (d) describe executive or administrative action, which is the domain of Mandamus or ordinary judicial review, and not Prohibition. (b) is wrong because courts cannot direct Parliament or a Legislature to pass or not pass a law. Only (c) matches the writ's nature.
explanations: Incorrect: Prohibition lies against judicial or quasi-judicial bodies, not against administrative officers. An officer's action is checked through Mandamus or other remedies.

Incorrect: Courts cannot compel or restrain a legislature from enacting a law through a writ. They can only review a law's validity after it is enacted. The word 'Prohibition' here is a pun on liquor prohibition and has no connection with the writ.
Correct: The writ is issued by a superior court to an inferior court or tribunal to stop proceedings that exceed its jurisdiction or violate natural justice.

Incorrect: Prohibition is not directed at the Government to stop an unconstitutional policy. Policies are challenged through judicial review, or through Mandamus or a declaration, and the Government is not a judicial body.
keyfact: Prohibition: issued by a higher court to a lower court or tribunal to stop proceedings (preventive, while the case is pending), whereas Certiorari quashes an order already passed.
summary: The answer is (c). A Writ of Prohibition is issued by a higher court (Supreme Court under Art. 32 or High Court under Art. 226) to a lower court or tribunal, directing it to stop proceedings in a case because it is acting beyond its jurisdiction or in violation of natural justice.

question:
Consider the following statements :
1. It is the Governor of the State who recognizes and declares any community of that State as a Scheduled Tribe. 87.
2. A community declared as a Scheduled Tribe in a State need not be so in another State. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
subject: Polity
detail: Article 342(1) empowers the President, after consulting the Governor where a State is concerned, to specify by public notification the tribes or tribal communities (or parts of or groups within them) deemed to be Scheduled Tribes in relation to that State or Union Territory. The Governor is only consulted and has no power to declare an ST. Under Article 342(2), only Parliament can include or exclude any community from the list through a law; a later notification cannot vary it. Article 366(25) defines Scheduled Tribes as those communities deemed so under Article 342. The lists are State-specific (or UT-specific), which is why a community can be an ST in one State and not in another, for example when migrants carry no ST status to a new State. The same logic applies to Scheduled Castes under Article 341. The Governor's role in Fifth Schedule areas is separate: he makes regulations for Scheduled Areas and does not declare STs. Elimination logic: statement 1 is wrong because the Governor does not declare STs, so options (a) and (c) fall. Statement 2 is right, so (d) is also out, leaving (b).
explanations: (a) is wrong because it treats statement 1 as correct. The Governor does not declare STs; the President does under Article 342.
(b) is right because statement 2 is correct (ST status is State-specific) and statement 1 is incorrect (the President specifies, not the Governor).
(c) is wrong because statement 1 is incorrect, so both cannot be correct.
(d) is wrong because statement 2 is correct, so at least one statement is right.
keyfact: Article 342: the President specifies STs (after consulting the Governor), only Parliament can modify the list, and the lists are State-specific.
statements: 1 — Incorrect: STs are specified by the President by public notification under Article 342 after consulting the Governor, and Parliament alone can alter the list. The Governor has no power to declare a community an ST.
2 — Correct: ST lists are specified State-wise or UT-wise, so a community notified as ST in one State need not be an ST in another.
summary: The answer is (b): only statement 2 is correct. Scheduled Tribes are specified by the President under Article 342, not by the Governor, and the specification is State-specific, so a community may be an ST in one State but not in another.

ocr: With reference to Union Budget, consider the following statements : 1. The Union Finance Minister on behalf of the Prime Minister lays the Annual Financial Statement before both the Houses of Parliament. At the Union level, no demand for a grant can be made except on_ the recommendation of the President of India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ? (a) 1 only 2 only (b) Both 1 and 2 (c) Neither 1 nor 2 (d)
subject: Polity
detail: The Union Budget is constitutionally the 'Annual Financial Statement' under Article 112, which the President causes to be laid before both Houses of Parliament for each financial year (1 April to 31 March). In practice the Union Finance Minister presents it, on behalf of the government headed by the Prime Minister, in the Lok Sabha and lays it before the Rajya Sabha. The Budget shows estimated receipts and expenditure, separating expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India (not voted by Parliament) from expenditure that is voted. Under Article 113, the charged expenditure may be discussed but not voted on, while other estimates are submitted to the Lok Sabha as 'demands for grants'. Article 113(3) provides that no demand for a grant shall be made except on the recommendation of the President. The Rajya Sabha can only discuss the Budget and has no power to vote on demands for grants. Money Bills, including the Appropriation Bill (Article 114) and Finance Bill, need the President's recommendation to be introduced, and only in the Lok Sabha. Elimination logic: since statement 2 is a textbook provision and statement 1 reflects the settled practice, both hold, so (c) follows.
explanations: (a) is wrong because it rejects statement 2, which is correct under Article 113(3).
(b) is wrong because it rejects statement 1, which correctly describes how the Budget is laid before both Houses by the Finance Minister.
(c) is right because both statements are correct: the Budget is laid before both Houses by the Finance Minister, and demands for grants need the President's recommendation.
(d) is wrong because at least one statement is correct, and in fact both are.
keyfact: Art. 112: Annual Financial Statement is laid before both Houses; Art. 113(3): no demand for a grant except on the President's recommendation.
statements: 1 — Correct: The Annual Financial Statement (Art. 112) is laid before both Houses. The Finance Minister does this on behalf of the government headed by the Prime Minister, and the President is constitutionally responsible for causing it to be laid.
2 — Correct: Under Article 113(3), no demand for a grant can be made except on the recommendation of the President.
summary: The answer is (c): both statements are correct. Article 112 requires the President to have the Annual Financial Statement (Budget) laid before both Houses, which in practice the Finance Minister does on the government's behalf. Article 113(2) bars any demand for a grant except on the President's recommendation.

ocr: Who of the following is the author of the books “The India Way” and “Why Bharat Matters” ? Bhupender Yadav (a) Nalin Mehta (b) Shashi Tharoor (c) Subrahmanyam Jaishankar (d)
subject: Current Affairs
detail: This is a current-affairs question on books by serving public figures, a recurring UPSC pattern. S. Jaishankar is a former career diplomat (IFS, 1977 batch) who served as Foreign Secretary (2015-18) and Ambassador to the USA, China, the Czech Republic and Singapore. He became External Affairs Minister in 2019 and is a Rajya Sabha member. 'The India Way: Strategies for an Uncertain World' (2020) argues that India must navigate multipolarity, balance relationships with major powers, and practise 'multi-alignment' and strategic autonomy. 'Why Bharat Matters' (2024) sets out India's foreign policy outlook and civilisational approach, with themes such as the Global South, the Neighbourhood First policy and the Indo-Pacific. Elimination logic: Bhupender Yadav is a Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change and is known for his legal and political work, not foreign-policy books. Nalin Mehta is an academic and author who writes on media, politics and sports. Shashi Tharoor is a prolific author, but his books are 'An Era of Darkness', 'The Great Indian Novel' and 'Pax Indica', and 'Pax Indica' is the one on foreign policy. The words 'Way' and 'Bharat' in the titles point to a foreign-policy author.
explanations: Incorrect: Bhupender Yadav is a Union Minister and BJP leader with a legal and political background; he did not write these books.
Incorrect: Nalin Mehta is an academic and author who writes on media, politics and sports; he is not the author of these two titles.
Incorrect: Shashi Tharoor is a well-known author, but his foreign-policy book is 'Pax Indica'; he did not write 'The India Way' or 'Why Bharat Matters'.
Correct: S. Jaishankar, External Affairs Minister, wrote 'The India Way' (2020) and 'Why Bharat Matters' (2024).
keyfact: S. Jaishankar (EAM, ex-Foreign Secretary) wrote 'The India Way' (2020) and 'Why Bharat Matters' (2024); Tharoor wrote 'Pax Indica'.
summary: The answer is (d) Subrahmanyam Jaishankar, India's External Affairs Minister since 2019. He wrote 'The India Way: Strategies for an Uncertain World' (2020) and 'Why Bharat Matters' (2024), both about India's foreign policy and its place in the world.

ocr: Consider the following pairs : Country Reason for being in the news 1. |Argentina | Worst economic crisis 2. |Sudan War between the country’s regular army and paramilitary forces 3. |Turkey Rescinded its membership of NATO How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched ? (a) Only one pair (b) Only two pairs All three pairs (c) (d) None of the pairs
subject: Current Affairs
detail: This is a current-affairs question on countries in the news in 2023. Argentina faced one of its worst economic crises in decades, with inflation above 100% annually, a depreciating peso, high poverty, and repeated IMF programmes; Javier Milei won the presidency in late 2023 on an economic-shock platform. Sudan has been in civil war since April 2023 between the Sudanese Armed Forces (led by Gen. Abdel Fattah al-Burhan) and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (led by Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo 'Hemedti'), causing a huge humanitarian and displacement crisis. Turkey has been a NATO member since 1952 and has never withdrawn; the 2023 news about Turkey concerned it delaying, and then ratifying (January 2024), Sweden's accession to NATO, after Finland joined in April 2023. NATO has no mechanism of 'rescinding' membership in practice, though Article 13 of the North Atlantic Treaty allows a member to withdraw after one year's notice. Elimination logic: once pair 3 is recognised as false and either of pairs 1 or 2 as true, the answer must be (b), since (c) and (d) are ruled out and (a) fails when both 1 and 2 are known to be true.
explanations: (a) is wrong: it would mean only one pair is correct, but both pair 1 (Argentina) and pair 2 (Sudan) are correct.
(b) is right: pairs 1 and 2 are correctly matched and pair 3 is false, so exactly two pairs are correct.
(c) is wrong: pair 3 is false because Turkey did not rescind its NATO membership.
(d) is wrong: Argentina's economic crisis and Sudan's army-RSF war are both correctly matched, so at least two pairs are right.
keyfact: Turkey has been in NATO since 1952 and never left (it ratified Sweden's accession in 2024); Sudan's war since April 2023 is SAF vs RSF.
statements: 1 — Correct: Argentina went through a severe economic crisis, with very high inflation, a falling peso, rising poverty and heavy IMF debt.
2 — Correct: Sudan has been in a war since April 2023 between the regular army (SAF) and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF).
3 — Incorrect: Turkey has been a NATO member since 1952 and has not withdrawn; the news was about its approval of Sweden's NATO accession.
summary: The correct answer is (b): only two pairs are correctly matched. Argentina's severe economic crisis (pair 1) and the Sudan army-versus-paramilitary (RSF) war (pair 2) are correct, while Turkey has never rescinded its NATO membership (pair 3).

question:
Consider the following statements : 91.
Statement-I : Sumed pipeline is a strategic route for Persian Gulf oil and natural gas shipments to Europe.
Statement-II : Sumed pipeline connects the Red Sea with the Mediterranean Sea. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements ?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-IT is correct
subject: Geography
detail: The SUMED pipeline (Arab Petroleum Pipeline Company) is an Egyptian crude oil pipeline, commissioned in 1977, running about 320 km from Ain Sukhna on the Gulf of Suez (Red Sea) to Sidi Kerir on the Mediterranean coast west of Alexandria. It consists of two parallel 42-inch lines and was built so that tankers too large for the Suez Canal could offload at Ain Sukhna, send oil through the pipeline, and reload at Sidi Kerir. It is also used as an alternative when the Canal is blocked, as in the 2021 Ever Given incident, and it is a key chokepoint-bypass route alongside the Suez Canal and Bab-el-Mandeb. Gulf producers such as Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Kuwait and Iraq ship crude via the Red Sea to Europe and the Mediterranean through it. The pipeline is owned by Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, the UAE and Qatar. Elimination logic: Statement-II is a geographic fact that is correct. Statement-I is correct as a strategic description. Because the Red Sea to Mediterranean connection is what allows Gulf oil to bypass the Canal and reach Europe, Statement-II explains Statement-I. This rules out (b), (c) and (d). Note that the pipeline mainly carries crude oil, and the question's wording follows the official key.
explanations: Right: both statements are correct and the Red Sea-Mediterranean link in Statement-II is the reason for the strategic role in Statement-I.
Wrong: although both statements are correct, Statement-II does directly explain Statement-I, so this option understates the relationship.
Wrong: Statement-II is correct, since the pipeline does connect the Red Sea with the Mediterranean.
Wrong: Statement-I is correct, since SUMED is a strategic route for Gulf oil going to Europe.
keyfact: SUMED: Ain Sukhna (Red Sea) to Sidi Kerir (Mediterranean), Egypt, about 320 km, since 1977, a Suez Canal bypass for Gulf oil going to Europe.
statements: 1 — Correct: SUMED is a strategic route that moves Persian Gulf oil to Europe via Egypt, bypassing or supplementing the Suez Canal.
2 — Correct: It runs from Ain Sukhna on the Red Sea (Gulf of Suez) to Sidi Kerir on the Mediterranean, and this connection explains why it serves as the strategic route in Statement-I.
summary: The correct answer is (a). The SUMED (Suez-Mediterranean) pipeline in Egypt links the Red Sea (Ain Sukhna) with the Mediterranean (Sidi Kerir, near Alexandria), and this link is exactly why it works as a strategic route for Gulf oil to reach Europe.

question:
Consider the following statements : 92.
1. The Red Sea receives very little precipitation in any form.
2. No water enters the Red Sea from rivers. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
subject: Geography
detail: The Red Sea lies between Africa (Egypt, Sudan, Eritrea) and the Arabian Peninsula (Saudi Arabia, Yemen), and is connected to the Mediterranean through the Suez Canal in the north and to the Gulf of Aden through the Bab-el-Mandeb strait in the south. It lies in the hot desert belt around the Tropic of Cancer, where subtropical high pressure and dry winds give very low rainfall, usually under about 200 mm a year, and extremely high evaporation, over 2 metres a year. No perennial river drains into it. The surrounding land is desert, and only seasonal wadis occasionally carry flash-flood water, which rarely reaches the sea. Because evaporation far exceeds precipitation and runoff, the water balance is made up by inflow from the Gulf of Aden through Bab-el-Mandeb. This gives the Red Sea very high salinity, about 36-41 parts per thousand, among the highest of any open sea. It is also one of the warmest seas and is a young, spreading rift basin. Elimination: since both facts are standard geography, any option that rejects either statement is wrong, leaving (c).
explanations: (a) Wrong: Statement 1 is correct, but statement 2 is also correct, so 'statement 1 only' is incomplete.
(b) Wrong: Statement 2 is correct, but statement 1 is also correct, so 'statement 2 only' is incomplete.
(c) Right: Both statements hold, since there is minimal precipitation and no river inflow, which is why the Red Sea is so saline.
(d) Wrong: Both statements are correct, so rejecting both is incorrect.
keyfact: The Red Sea has almost no rainfall and no rivers flowing into it, so it is highly saline (about 36-41 ppt) and is replenished through Bab-el-Mandeb.
statements: 1 — Correct: The Red Sea lies in a hot desert region with very low rainfall and very high evaporation.
2 — Correct: No permanent river enters the Red Sea; only occasional seasonal wadis, so rivers contribute effectively no inflow.
summary: The correct answer is (c): both statements are correct. The Red Sea lies in an arid zone with very little rainfall and no rivers flowing into it, so evaporation far exceeds inflow, making it one of the saltiest seas.

question: According to the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), which one of the following is the largest source of sulphur dioxide emissions ?
subject: Environment
detail: Sulphur dioxide is a colourless gas with a sharp odour, belonging to the group of sulphur oxides (SOx). It forms when sulphur-bearing fuels such as coal and oil are burned. The US EPA states that the largest source of SO2 in the atmosphere is fossil fuel combustion at power plants (about 73% in its older inventories) and other industrial facilities. Smaller sources include industrial processes such as extracting metal from ore, and natural sources such as volcanoes. Mobile sources, namely locomotives, large ships and other non-road equipment that burn high-sulphur fuel, contribute still less. Coal contains sulphur as an impurity, so thermal power stations release large volumes of SO2 through their flue gas. SO2 causes respiratory problems, forms acid rain (with NOx) and contributes to secondary PM2.5 formation. In India, flue gas desulphurisation (FGD) units are being mandated for thermal plants to cut SO2, and the National Ambient Air Quality Standards set limits for SO2 (50 µg/m3 annual, 80 µg/m3 for 24 hours). Elimination logic: options (a), (b) and (c) are real but secondary sources, so the single largest source is the stationary combustion of fossil fuels in power plants.
explanations: Incorrect: Locomotives burning fossil fuels emit SO2, but they are a small share of the total compared with power generation.
Incorrect: Ships burning high-sulphur marine fuel are a notable source, especially near ports, but they are not the largest overall source.
Incorrect: Extracting metals from ores (smelting) releases SO2, but the EPA ranks it as a minor industrial source behind fossil-fuel power generation.
Correct: The EPA identifies fossil fuel combustion at power plants, mainly coal-fired, as the largest source of SO2 emissions.
keyfact: Largest anthropogenic SO2 source per EPA: fossil-fuel (mainly coal) combustion in power plants; SO2 causes acid rain and secondary PM2.5.
summary: The answer is (d) Power plants using fossil fuels. According to the US EPA, the burning of fossil fuels, mainly coal, by power plants and other industrial facilities is the largest source of sulphur dioxide (SO2) emissions.

question:
Consider the following statements :
Statement-I : There is instability and worsening security situation in the Sahel region.
Statement-II : There have been military takeovers/coups d’état in several countries of the Sahel region in the recent past. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements ?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
subject: Current Affairs
detail: The Sahel is the semi-arid belt south of the Sahara, running from Senegal and Mauritania in the west to Sudan and Eritrea in the east. The core of the crisis is Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger, Chad and Mauritania. Jihadist groups linked to Al-Qaeda (JNIM) and the Islamic State (ISGS/ISWAP) operate there, alongside ethnic conflict, weak state presence, poverty and climate stress. Mali had coups in 2020 and 2021, Burkina Faso in January and September 2022, Niger in July 2023, and Chad's military took over in 2021. Guinea (2021) and Gabon (2023) also saw coups, though they are not Sahelian. The juntas expelled French forces (Operation Barkhane ended), pushed out the UN mission MINUSMA in Mali, and weakened the G5 Sahel force. Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger left ECOWAS and formed the Alliance of Sahel States (AES), and some turned towards Russia (Wagner/Africa Corps). Violence, displacement and civilian deaths have risen. Elimination logic: both statements are factually true, so (c) and (d) fail. The coups are a major cause of the security vacuum and a symptom of the crisis, so the link is explanatory and (b) fails.
explanations: Correct: both statements are true, and the coups, by dismantling civilian governance and security alliances, directly contributed to the worsening security situation.

Wrong: it accepts that both statements are true but denies the causal link. Coups and insecurity feed each other, as juntas justified takeovers by failures against insurgents and then weakened the regional security architecture.
Wrong: Statement-II is true, since there have been several coups in Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger and Chad.
Wrong: Statement-I is true, since the region is widely recognised as the global epicentre of terrorism and instability.
keyfact: Sahel coups: Mali 2020/21, Burkina Faso 2022 (x2), Niger 2023; these three formed the Alliance of Sahel States and left ECOWAS.
statements: 1 — Correct: The Sahel has seen rising jihadist violence, displacement and weakening state control, especially in Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger.

2 — Correct: Mali (2020, 2021), Burkina Faso (2022 twice), Niger (2023) and Chad (2021) saw military takeovers. Statement-II explains Statement-I because the coups disrupted governance and counter-terror cooperation, and ended Western and UN security partnerships.
summary: The answer is (a). Both statements are correct, and the coups explain the instability: military takeovers in Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger have weakened governance, disrupted counter-insurgency cooperation and worsened the security situation in the Sahel.

question:
Consider the following statements :
Statement-I : India does not import apples from the United States of America.
Statement-II : In India, the law prohibits the import of Genetically Modified food without the approval of the competent authority. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements ?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I : ;
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does noé¢ explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
subject: Economy
detail: Statement-I is factually wrong. The USA has long been an apple exporter to India, and India has imported US apples for years. Until 2023 they faced a heavy tariff (50% basic customs duty plus other levies). In June 2023, during the Prime Minister's visit to the USA, India withdrew the retaliatory additional 20% duty on US apples, among other products, as part of settling the WTO disputes. This made US apples cheaper and increased their imports. Statement-II is correct. The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (Section 22) and the FSSAI's regulations on genetically modified foods prohibit the manufacture, sale, import or use of GM food without approval. Under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 and the Rules of 1989, the Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee (GEAC) under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change is the approving authority for GM organisms. The FSSAI regulates the import of GM food in accordance with the 2022 Genetically Modified Foods Regulations. Elimination logic: once Statement-I is seen to be false, options (a), (b) and (c), which all treat it as correct, fall away, which leaves (d).
explanations: (a) is wrong because Statement-I is incorrect, since India does import US apples, so Statement-II cannot explain it.
(b) is wrong because it treats Statement-I as correct, but India does import apples from the USA.
(c) is wrong because it says Statement-I is correct and Statement-II is incorrect, which is the reverse of the facts.
(d) is right because Statement-I is false (India imports US apples) and Statement-II is true (GM food imports need approval from the competent authority).
keyfact: India imports US apples (extra 20% duty withdrawn in 2023), while GM food imports need FSSAI/GEAC approval under the FSS Act, 2006 and the EP Act, 1986.
statements: 1 — Incorrect: India does import apples from the USA, and the 2023 withdrawal of the additional 20% duty made these imports cheaper.

2 — Correct: Under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and the FSSAI's GM food regulations, GM food imports need approval from the competent authority, with GEAC approval for GMOs under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
summary: The answer is (d): Statement-I is incorrect and Statement-II is correct. India does import apples from the USA (after tariff concessions in 2023), and the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 requires approval for GM food imports.

question:
With reference to the Speaker of the 95. Lok Sabha, consider the following statements : While any resolution for the removal of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha is under consideration
1. He/She shall not preside.
2. He/She shall not have the right to speak. 83. He/She shall not be entitled to vote on the resolution in the first instance. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
subject: Polity
detail: Article 94 provides that the Speaker vacates office on ceasing to be a member of the House, by resigning in writing to the Deputy Speaker, or by removal through a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the House (an effective majority). At least 14 days' notice of the resolution is required. Article 96 governs the Speaker's position while such a resolution is under consideration. Clause (1) says the Speaker shall not preside at any sitting, though the Deputy Speaker or another person presides in his or her place. Clause (2) says the Speaker has the right to speak in, and otherwise take part in, the proceedings of the House, and, notwithstanding Article 100, can vote only in the first instance on the resolution or any other matter during such proceedings, but not in the case of an equality of votes. So the Speaker keeps the right to speak and the right to vote in the first instance; there is no casting vote. This contrasts with normal sittings, where the Speaker votes only to break a tie. Elimination: statements 2 and 3 are wrong, so only (a) survives.
explanations: Correct: statement 1 is the only one that holds, since the Speaker cannot preside but retains the rights to speak and to vote in the first instance.
Wrong: it counts statement 2 as correct, but the Speaker has the right to speak under Article 96(2).
Wrong: it counts statements 2 and 3 as correct, but both contradict Article 96(2).
